--- name: quartz description: Quartz design system rules for this project's UI. Use when building or changing any screen, component, form or style, when porting an existing screen onto Quartz, or when checking UI against Quartz. --- # Quartz Black and white chassis with five muted kind hues and warm trouble colors, for AI support products and agent consoles. ## Setup Once, in the root layout: put the "quartz" class on `` or the root element of the UI, with `QuartzPortalProvider` inside it. Quartz's styles and tokens apply only inside that class. Menus, dialogs, popovers and toasts render at the end of the body; QuartzPortalProvider keeps them inside the scope, and without it they lose every token. `import {QuartzPortalProvider} from '@/lib/quartz/portal'` `{children}` ## Steps 1. For a whole screen, start from a block under Blocks when one fits: install it, then swap its sample data and copy for the real ones. 2. Pick the components the screen needs from the index below. Fetch each one's page before using it: it has the props, variants and that component's rules. 3. Build only from those components and the tokens under Tokens, inside an element with the "quartz" class. Import each from the path in the index; support pieces are under Imports. Dark mode: put data-theme="dark" or the class dark on the quartz element or any ancestor, such as . The theme does not follow the system setting (prefers-color-scheme) on its own. 4. Frame the screen with the Page shell. If a component is missing, build the stand-in under Coverage gaps; if none is listed, compose it from existing components and tokens and say what you built. Never invent a token. 5. Ask the person when the screen needs a credential, an environment, the object of a destructive action or an approval policy you were not given; never invent a key, an endpoint or which tools need approval. Decide layout, copy and components from these rules and say what you chose. 6. Porting an existing screen: swap one piece at a time for its component, keep the behavior and copy, and delete the old styles once nothing uses them. For a whole app, run migrate-design-system when it is installed. 7. Lint: install it once with `npx shadcn@latest add https://design.how/r/quartz/lint.json`, then run `npx eslint -c quartz.eslint.config.mjs .`. Each message names the fix. 8. Review before you finish: run the lint and fix every error, then render the screen at 390 and 1280 wide, check it against the global rules and the anti-slop list, fix the worst defect, and check again. Done when no MUST or NEVER is broken and no raw color, size or font is left. Run ui-review when it is installed. ## Priority order When rules conflict, the earlier item wins. 1. Accessibility and keyboard behavior 2. Tokens, never raw values 3. Existing components, never rebuilt 4. Layout and spacing scale 5. Polish: motion, radius, details ## Global rules 1. quartz-components-first MUST Use a component from this system before writing custom markup. Because hand-built markup skips the component's focus ring, keyboard handling and states, which people notice one at a time. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `

Because one word for one question lets a person guess the prop on a component they have not used, and tone, kind or variant for a state sends them to the docs. 7. quartz-fields-not-lines SHOULD Separate containers with a grey field; use a hairline only where a field cannot. Because boxes inside bordered boxes stack lines until the groups blur. 8. quartz-keyboard MUST Keep every control keyboard-operable with a visible focus ring and an accessible name. Because a keyboard user loses their place without the ring, and a screen reader announces an unnamed icon button as "button". - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 9. quartz-ask-before-destructive MUST Stop an agent before a destructive or irreversible action with a ToolCall awaiting permission and Deny and Allow; save typed confirmation for deleting for good a thing that holds others, such as a project (dialog-typed-confirm-irreversible). Because a prompt release, a deleted key or a sent reply cannot be taken back, and a typed name on every action trains people to type through the real one. - Correct: `}/>` 10. quartz-ai-turn MUST Build a turn inside Conversation from AgentTurn, ToolCallList, Response and ConversationTail, with PromptQueue above PromptInput; only the running tool row shows the arc. Because each part owns one job, and a second spinner or phrase in the turn makes the thread say two things at once. - Correct: ```tsx {text}{done && {actions}} {waiting && } ``` 11. quartz-sentence-case MUST Write sentence case, plain labels, verb plus object on actions. Because title case reads as proper nouns, and a bare OK or Submit does not say what the press will do. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 12. quartz-no-decoration NEVER Add shadows on flat things, gradients, glass, pills, side bars or looping motion. Because each one competes with the status words and kind labels that carry meaning, and glass drops text contrast. - Correct: `` - Wrong: `` 13. quartz-smallest-change SHOULD Make the smallest change; do not add files or abstractions that were not requested. Because every extra file is code the person has to review and keep. 14. quartz-stop-when-missing MUST Stop and say so when a component or token is missing; do not invent one. Because an invented token resolves to nothing and renders unstyled, and an invented component never gets the system's fixes. ## Page shell Every screen sits in this frame. - Root: the `` from quartz-scope, which sets the page color, text and font; in its QuartzPortalProvider, `` holding `Sidebar` (`--sidebar` wide, a sheet under 768px) and `SidebarInset`, the page's `main` - Top bar, first in SidebarInset: `

Details: https://design.how/systems/quartz/foundations/anti-slop.md - anti-slop-no-caps NEVER Set text in capitals or tracked out; keep sentence case. Because capitals read slower and make every label shout, so a real warning no longer stands out. - Wrong: `Running` - anti-slop-mono-for-copyable MUST Set mono only for code, commands, paths, IDs, keys and hashes; numbers get the data utility. Because mono marks what a person copies, so a mono duration looks like an id. - anti-slop-no-em-dash NEVER Use an em dash for a pause or an empty value; end the sentence, or write None.
